result.summary: This contract is a one-sided agreement under which you will design and build a website for Northwind Digital Ltd. The terms heavily favor the client, featuring an unlimited liability clause, a strict 24-month global non-compete, and a 90-day payment delay. Additionally, the client reserves the right to cancel the agreement immediately and change the contract terms unilaterally.

quote.text: This Agreement is made on 1 October 2026
This Agreement lasts for twelve (12) months and renews automatically for further twelve-month periods
The Contractor may terminate on ninety (90) days' written notice
This Agreement is governed by the laws of England and Wales

obligations.description: Design and build the client's website in accordance with the project brief.

quote.text: The Contractor will design and build the Client's customer website as described in the project brief

obligations.description: Maintain the confidentiality of the client's information during the contract and indefinitely after it ends.

quote.text: The Contractor must keep the Client's information confidential during this Agreement and for an unlimited period afterwards

obligations.description: Pay the contractor's invoices within 90 days of receipt.

quote.text: The Client will pay the Fees within ninety (90) days of receiving a valid invoice

risks.title: Uncompensated Scope Changes
risks.plain_language: The client can change what they want you to do at any point, but your pay will not increase unless they agree to it in writing.
risks.why_it_matters: You could be forced to perform significant extra work for no additional pay if the client unilaterally modifies the scope of the project.

quotes.text: The Client may change the scope of the Services at any time by written notice. The Fees will not change unless the Client agrees otherwise in writing

risks.title: Unfettered Right to Withhold Payment
risks.plain_language: The client can refuse to pay your invoices if they are not satisfied with your work deliverables.
risks.why_it_matters: The client can withhold your money based on purely subjective opinions about your work, with no clear independent standard of quality or evaluation process.

quotes.text: The Client may withhold any payment if it is not satisfied with the Deliverables

risks.title: Loss of Pre-existing Intellectual Property
risks.plain_language: All rights in your work, including templates, tools, or materials you owned before starting this contract, are transferred to the client upon creation.
risks.why_it_matters: You lose the rights to your own background IP and reusable codebase. You will not be able to legally use your own pre-existing materials for future clients.

quotes.text: All rights in the Deliverables, including any pre-existing materials of the Contractor used in them, are assigned to the Client on creation

risks.title: Worldwide Non-Compete Restriction
risks.plain_language: For two years after the contract ends, you cannot work for any business that competes with the client anywhere in the world.
risks.why_it_matters: This is a exceptionally restrictive non-compete. It could prevent you from taking freelance work or jobs in your industry globally, locking you out of your career field.

quotes.text: For twenty-four (24) months after this Agreement ends, the Contractor will not provide services to any business that competes with the Client anywhere in the world

risks.title: Unlimited Financial Liability and Indemnity
risks.plain_language: You are fully liable for all losses the client experiences from your services, and you must cover all costs if a third party sues the client over your work.
risks.why_it_matters: You have unlimited financial risk. A simple error or an intellectual property claim from a third party could lead to massive expenses, potentially bankrupting you.

quotes.text: The Contractor is liable for all losses suffered by the Client arising from the Services, without limit
The Contractor will indemnify the Client against any claim by a third party relating to the Deliverables

risks.title: One-Sided Immediate Termination
risks.plain_language: The client can fire you immediately at any time, but you must give 90 days' notice. Upon termination, they will only pay for accepted deliverables.
risks.why_it_matters: You could be dismissed instantly without compensation for mid-milestone work, while you remain locked in for three months if you decide to resign.

quotes.text: The Client may terminate this Agreement at any time with immediate effect. The Contractor may terminate on ninety (90) days' written notice
On termination the Client will pay only for Deliverables it has accepted

risks.title: Unilateral Contract Changes
risks.plain_language: The client can change the terms of this contract by posting updates on a portal, and your continued work acts as agreement to those changes.
risks.why_it_matters: The client can unilaterally change crucial elements—such as your fees, obligations, or deadlines—without your signature or active consent.

quotes.text: The Client may update these terms by posting a new version on its supplier portal. Continued work by the Contractor means acceptance

risks.title: Severe Penalty for Late Invoicing
risks.plain_language: You must submit your invoices within 14 days of finishing a milestone; late submissions will not be paid.
risks.why_it_matters: If you experience an administrative oversight or minor delay in sending an invoice, you lose the entire payment for that milestone with no recourse.

quotes.text: Invoices must be submitted within 14 days of completing a milestone; late invoices will not be paid

risks.title: Portfolio Restrictions
risks.plain_language: You are not allowed to display any of your work for this project in your portfolio without prior written consent.
risks.why_it_matters: This makes it highly difficult to showcase your skills and market yourself to future prospective clients.

quotes.text: The Contractor may not show the Deliverables in a portfolio without the Client's prior written consent

risks.title: Class-Action Waiver
risks.plain_language: You give up the right to bring or participate in any class or collective legal action against the client.
risks.why_it_matters: If multiple contractors face systematic payment defaults or legal issues from this client, you cannot join forces to sue them collectively.

quotes.text: The Contractor waives any right to bring or join a class or collective action

missing_or_unclear: Schedule A (which contains the actual fee rates and amounts) is referenced but is not attached to this document.
The 'project brief' describing the scope of services is referenced but not included.
There is no provision for late-payment interest to protect you against delayed invoices.
A definition of what businesses qualify as a 'competitor' under the non-compete clause is missing.
An objective test or review process for payment acceptance is missing from the document.
questions_for_lawyer: Under English law, is the 24-month worldwide non-compete clause (Clause 6.1) enforceable, and can we draft a much narrower, local alternative?
How can we modify Clause 7.1 to cap my total financial liability at a multiple of the fees paid under the contract (e.g., 100% of fees paid)?
How can we carve out my background and pre-existing IP in Clause 4.1 so that I retain ownership and merely grant the client a non-exclusive license?
Can we change Clause 9.1 so that any amendments to this contract must be written and signed by both parties, rather than unilaterally posted on a portal?
Can we amend Clause 3.2 to establish an objective standard of 'reasonable quality' and a cure period for deliverables, rather than letting the client withhold pay at their discretion?
next_steps: Request the missing documents (Schedule A and the Project Brief) to review the financial terms and your exact scope of work.
Draft written markups of the contract to address key high-risk areas, focusing on capping your liability, limiting the non-compete, and deleting the unilateral amendment clause.
Submit the proposed changes to the client for negotiation.

If the client refuses to negotiate on critical issues like unlimited liability, unilateral portal updates, or the non-compete, determine whether you can accept these severe business risks before signing next week.

disclaimer: This is information about the text you provided, not legal advice. It doesn't know your local law, your negotiating position, or anything outside the document, and it can be wrong.
